### 🟡 Changes recommended Snapshot emission can lose telemetry semantics for generic Log4j `MapMessage` implementations.
1 open finding - [Preserve generic MapMessage semantics during replay snapshotting](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-java-instrumentation/pull/20523#discussion_r4244494175) · New
What changed in this PR Reduces appender read-lock scope during pre-installation log capture. **Changes:** - Captures replay snapshots before locking. - Prints overflow warnings after unlocking. - Reuses Log4j snapshots when installation completes during capture. | File | Description | | ---- | ----------- | | Logback `OpenTelemetryAppender.java` | Narrows replay lock scope and defers warnings. | | Log4j `OpenTelemetryAppender.java` | Narrows lock scope and reuses captured events. |
🧠 **Review effort:** Balanced --- 💡 Add a `code-review` agent skill or configure MCP servers for context-aware, tailored reviews. Learn more in the docs.

[General] This transition path now changes telemetry for supported `MapMessage` implementations other than `StringMapMessage` and `StructuredDataMessage`. `LogEventToReplay` wraps those other map messages in `MessageCopy`, so `LogEventMapper` no longer recognizes them as a `MapMessage` and loses their event name, map body rules, and structured attributes when installation completes during capture. Please preserve generic `MapMessage` semantics in the snapshot (or emit the original event in this branch).

Builds on #20519 to further reduce the read-lock scope in the Logback and Log4j appenders. Replay-event capture runs on the original logging thread before locking, and the queue-overflow warning prints after unlocking.

The installation recheck, buffer-versus-emit decision, and once-only warning claim remain protected by the existing lock. If installation finishes during Log4j capture, emission reuses the snapshot to avoid formatting the original message again. The initialized fast path remains lock-free.

Part of the locking audit in #20000.
metadata.title: Reduce appender read-lock scope for replay capture
